newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies may be nervous after storage data.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies may be nervous after storage data.

text.p: Strong export demand may offset initial bearish sentiment from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's cold storage data for pork bellies, and pork belly futures trade could be nervous on Monday, analysts said.

Although first indications point to a lower start in CME pork bellies on Monday following the USDA report of 54.8 million lbs of frozen pork bellies in storage, analysts were reluctant to say that futures would stay lower in view of recent strong export demand for bellies.

The belly stocks compared with analysts' forecasts for 49.0 million to 53.2 million lbs. Early indications were for pork belly futures to open 0.500 to 1.000 cent lower, but prices could later turn back up.

"Instead of the people who have the non-reporting warehouses putting three million pounds of bellies away during the month, they put five million pounds away," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Rich Tokheim of Investment Research Co, who had been looking for the low side of early estimates, was surprised by the large stocks, which likely indicated slow domestic demand for bacon.
"We're eight million (lbs) above a year ago and the kill this year has been significantly lower, so (domestic) demand is lower," Tokheim said.

But analysts noted that recent developments in exports, especially to Japan, along with a pace of storing so far in April that has been much lighter than a year ago, may still be the main influence in belly futures Monday. Belly futures ran up to contract highs Friday and the highest price levels for any contract since last August when the all time high of 105.250 cents was established.

"If the futures are 100 or 150 points (1.00 to 1.50 cents) lower on Monday and there are not a whole lot of offerings on the fresh market at that moment, the futures will come right back," Levitt said.
Not only is Japan in the market for bellies but there has been talk of interest from Canada and possibly from South Korea as well, Levitt said.
"I still see this (futures) market rallying into May," Tokheim said.
